sanskrit: tam evaṃ śokasaṃtaptaṃ bharataṃ kekayīsutam uvāca vadatāṃ śreṣṭho vasiṣṭhaḥ śreṣṭhavāg ṛṣiḥ
english: To Bharata, son of Kaikeyī, who was thus consumed by grief, spoke Vasiṣṭha, foremost among speakers, a sage of most excellent speech.

sanskrit: alaṃ śokena bhadraṃ te rājaputra mahāyaśaḥ prāptakālaṃ narapateḥ kuru saṃyānam uttaram
english: "Enough of grief — may it be well with you, O prince of great renown. Perform now the final last rites due to the king in their proper time."

sanskrit: vasiṣṭhasya vacaḥ śrutvā bharato dhāraṇāṃ gataḥ pretakāryāṇi sarvāṇi kārayām āsa dharmavit
english: Hearing the words of Vasiṣṭha, Bharata composed himself; and he, versed in dharma, caused all the funerary rites to be performed.

sanskrit: uddhṛtaṃ tailasaṃkledāt sa tu bhūmau niveśitam āpītavarṇavadanaṃ prasuptam iva bhūmipam
english: The king, his face pale and sallow in hue, was lifted out of the oil vessel and laid upon the ground, as if merely asleep.

sanskrit: niveśya śayane cāgrye nānāratnapariṣkṛte tato daśarathaṃ putro vilalāpa suduḥkhitaḥ
english: Having placed Daśaratha upon a splendid couch adorned with many jewels, his son lamented in deepest sorrow.

sanskrit: kiṃ te vyavasitaṃ rājan proṣite mayy anāgate vivāsya rāmaṃ dharmajñaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ ca mahābalam
english: "What was your resolve, O king — while I was away and had not yet returned — to banish Rāma, who knows dharma, and the mighty Lakṣmaṇa?

sanskrit: kva yāsyasi mahārāja hitvemaṃ duḥkhitaṃ janam hīnaṃ puruṣasiṃhena rāmeṇākliṣṭakarmaṇā
english: "Where will you go, O great king, abandoning this afflicted people, now bereft of Rāma the lion among men, whose deeds are ever effortless?"

sanskrit: yogakṣemaṃ tu te rājan ko 'smin kalpayitā pure tvayi prayāte svas tāta rāme ca vanam āśrite
english: "Who, O king, will provide for the welfare and security of this city now that you have departed, dear father, and Rāma has taken refuge in the forest?"

sanskrit: vidhavā pṛthivī rājaṃs tvayā hīnā na rājate hīnacandreva rajanī nagarī pratibhāti mām
english: "The earth, O king, bereft of you, shines no more — it is widowed. The city appears to me as a night without the moon."

sanskrit: evaṃ vilapamānaṃ taṃ bharataṃ dīnamānasaṃ abravīd vacanaṃ bhūyo vasiṣṭhas tu mahān ṛṣiḥ
english: To Bharata lamenting thus, his mind cast down in sorrow, the great sage Vasiṣṭha again spoke these words.

sanskrit: pretakāryāṇi yāny asya kartavyāni viśāmpateḥ tāny avyagraṃ mahābāho kriyatām avicāritam
english: "Whatever funerary rites are to be performed for this lord of the people — let them be carried out without delay and without hesitation, O mighty-armed one."

sanskrit: tatheti bharato vākyaṃ vasiṣṭhasyābhipūjya tat ṛtvikpurohitācāryāṃs tvarayām āsa sarvaśaḥ
english: Saying "So be it" and honouring the word of Vasiṣṭha, Bharata urged on in all matters the officiating priests, the family chaplain, and the ācāryas.

sanskrit: ye tv agrato narendrasya agny agārād bahiṣkṛtāḥ ṛtvigbhir yājakaiś caiva te hriyante yathāvidhi
english: Those sacred fires that had been taken out from the fire-house before the king were now carried in due ritual order by the officiating priests and sacrificers.

sanskrit: śibilāyām athāropya rājānaṃ gatacetanam bāṣpakaṇṭhā vimanasas tam ūhuḥ paricārakāḥ
english: Placing the king, now devoid of consciousness, upon the funeral bier, his attendants — their throats choked with tears and their minds distraught — bore him forth.

sanskrit: hiraṇyaṃ ca suvarṇaṃ ca vāsāṃsi vividhāni ca prakiranto janā mārgaṃ nṛpater agrato yayuḥ
english: Scattering silver and gold and garments of many kinds, the people went along the road before the king.

sanskrit: candanāguruniryāsān saralaṃ padmakaṃ tathā devadārūṇi cāhṛtya citāṃ cakrus tathāpare
english: Others brought sandalwood and fragrant resins of aguru, the sarala pine, padmaka wood, and devadāru, and with these they built the funeral pyre.

sanskrit: gandhān uccāvacāṃś cānyāṃs tatra dattvātha bhūmipam tataḥ saṃveśayām āsuś citāmadhye tam ṛtvijaḥ
english: Having placed fragrant substances of various high and low kinds thereon, the officiating priests then laid the lord of the earth in the centre of the pyre.

sanskrit: tathā hutāśanaṃ hutvā jepus tasya tadartvijaḥ jaguś ca te yathāśāstraṃ tatra sāmāni sāmagāḥ
english: Having offered oblations to the sacred fire, the priests recited their sacred formulas for him; and the Sāma-singers chanted the Sāma hymns there in accordance with the scriptures.

sanskrit: śibikābhiś ca yānaiś ca yathārhaṃ tasya yoṣitaḥ nagarān niryayus tatra vṛddhaiḥ parivṛtās tadā
english: The royal women, in palanquins and conveyances befitting their station, went forth from the city, escorted by elders.

sanskrit: prasavyaṃ cāpi taṃ cakrur ṛtvijo 'gnicitaṃ nṛpam striyaś ca śokasaṃtaptāḥ kausalyā pramukhās tadā
english: The officiating priests performed the pradakṣiṇā in the reverse direction around the king lying on the fire-heaped pyre; and the women, consumed by grief, with Kausalyā at their head, did likewise.

sanskrit: krauñcīnām iva nārīṇāṃ ninādas tatra śuśruve ārtānāṃ karuṇaṃ kāle krośantīnāṃ sahasraśaḥ
english: The wailing of the women there was heard — piteous and sorrowful at that hour — like the cries of female krauñca birds, thousands of them crying out in anguish.

sanskrit: tato rudantyo vivaśā vilapya ca punaḥ punaḥ yānebhyaḥ sarayūtīram avaterur varāṅganāḥ
english: Then the noble women, weeping, helpless, and lamenting again and again, descended from their conveyances at the bank of the Sarayū.

sanskrit: kṛtodakaṃ te bharatena sārdhaṃ nṛpāṅganā mantripurohitāś ca puraṃ praviśyāśruparītanetrā bhūmau daśāhaṃ vyanayanta duḥkham
english: Having performed the water-offerings together with Bharata, the royal women, ministers, and the family priest re-entered the city with eyes flooded with tears and spent ten days lying on the ground in their grief.

sanskrit: tato daśāhe 'tigate kṛtaśauco nṛpātmajaḥ dvādaśe 'hani saṃprāpte śrāddhakarmāṇy akārayat
english: Then, when the ten days had passed, the prince, having completed the purification rites, caused the śrāddha ceremonies to be performed on the twelfth day.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇebhyo dadau ratnaṃ dhanam annaṃ ca puṣkalam bāstikaṃ bahuśuklaṃ ca gāś cāpi śataśas tathā
english: He gave to the brāhmaṇas gems, wealth, and abundant food; and also bāstika grain, much white cloth, and cows by the hundreds.

sanskrit: dāsīdāsaṃ ca yānaṃ ca veśmāni sumahānti ca brāhmaṇebhyo dadau putro rājñas tasyaurdhvadaihikam
english: The son of the king gave to the brāhmaṇas female and male servants, vehicles, and great mansions as the post-mortem offerings for his father.

sanskrit: tataḥ prabhātasamaye divase 'tha trayodaśe vilalāpa mahābāhur bharataḥ śokamūrchitaḥ
english: Then, at the time of dawn on the thirteenth day, the mighty-armed Bharata lamented, overwhelmed and faint with grief.

sanskrit: śabdāpihitakaṇṭhaś ca śodhanārtham upāgataḥ citāmūle pitur vākyam idam āha suduḥkhitaḥ
english: With voice choked by sobbing, having come there for the purification rites, he stood at the foot of his father's pyre and spoke these words in deepest sorrow.

sanskrit: tāta yasmin niṣṛṣṭo 'haṃ tvayā bhrātari rāghave tasmin vanaṃ pravrajite śūnye tyakto 'smy ahaṃ tvayā
english: "O father, that brother Rāghava to whose care you entrusted me has gone away to the forest — and thus, bereft of him, I am left desolate by you."

sanskrit: yathāgatir anāthāyāḥ putraḥ pravrājito vanam tām ambāṃ tāta kausalyāṃ tyaktvā tvaṃ kva gato nṛpa
english: "Her son has been sent away to the forest, leaving her without refuge — abandoning that mother Kausalyā, O father, where have you gone, O king?"

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā bhasmāruṇaṃ tac ca dagdhāsthisthānamaṇḍalam pituḥ śarīra nirvāṇaṃ niṣṭanan viṣasāda ha
english: Beholding that reddish-grey ash, the circle of the place where his father's bones had been burned, he groaned and sank down, devastated, at the extinction of his father's body.

sanskrit: sa tu dṛṣṭvā rudan dīnaḥ papāta dharaṇītale utthāpyamānaḥ śakrasya yantra dhvaja iva cyutaḥ
english: Weeping, wretched, he fell to the ground; and as they raised him up he was like the ceremonial banner of Indra toppling from its post.

sanskrit: abhipetus tataḥ sarve tasyāmātyāś śucivratam antakāle nipatitaṃ yayātim ṛṣayo yathā
english: Then all his ministers rushed to him — as sages rush to Yayāti, that pure-vowed king, when he falls at the time of death.

sanskrit: śatrughnaś cāpi bharataṃ dṛṣṭvā śokapariplutam visaṃjño nyapatad bhūmau bhūmipālam anusmaran
english: Śatrughna too, seeing Bharata overwhelmed by grief, lost consciousness and fell to the ground, remembering their father the protector of the earth.

sanskrit: unmatta iva niścetā vilalāpa suduḥkhitaḥ smṛtvā pitur guṇāṅgāni tāni tāni tadā tadā
english: Like one deranged, bereft of his senses, he lamented in deepest sorrow, recalling again and again those many virtues and qualities of his father.

sanskrit: mantharā prabhavas tīvraḥ kaikeyīgrāhasaṃkulaḥ varadānamayo 'kṣobhyo 'majjayac chokasāgaraḥ
english: A fierce ocean of grief — its source Mantharā, its current the grasping of Kaikeyī, its waves the granting of the boon — immeasurable and impassable, engulfed them.

sanskrit: sukumāraṃ ca bālaṃ ca satataṃ lālitaṃ tvayā kva tāta bharataṃ hitvā vilapantaṃ gato bhavān
english: "O father, this Bharata who is tender and young, always fondly indulged by you — leaving him here weeping, where have you gone?"

sanskrit: nanu bhojyeṣu pāneṣu vastreṣv ābharaṇeṣu ca pravārayasi naḥ sarvāṃs tan naḥ ko 'dya kariṣyati
english: "Did you not always freely offer us food, drink, garments, and ornaments — who will do that for us now?"

sanskrit: avadāraṇa kāle tu pṛthivī nāvadīryate vihīnā yā tvayā rājñā dharmajñena mahātmanā
english: "Now surely is the time for the earth to split asunder, yet it does not split — it that is bereft of you, the king who knew dharma, the great-souled one."

sanskrit: pitari svargam āpanne rāme cāraṇyam āśrite kiṃ me jīvita sāmarthyaṃ pravekṣyāmi hutāśanam
english: "With my father having attained heaven and Rāma having taken refuge in the forest, what purpose does my life serve? I shall enter the sacred fire."

sanskrit: hīno bhrātrā ca pitrā ca śūnyām ikṣvākupālitām ayodhyāṃ na pravekṣyāmi pravekṣyāmi tapovanam
english: "Bereft of both brother and father, I will not enter Ayodhyā — that city once guarded by the Ikṣvākus — now empty; I will enter the hermitage forest."

sanskrit: tayor vilapitaṃ śrutvā vyasanaṃ cānvavekṣya tat bhṛśam ārtatarā bhūyaḥ sarva evānugāminaḥ
english: Hearing the laments of those two and witnessing their calamity, all those who followed them were all the more stricken and afflicted.

sanskrit: tato viṣaṇṇau śrāntau ca śatrughnabharatāv ubhau dharaṇyāṃ saṃvyaceṣṭetāṃ bhagnaśṛṅgāv ivarṣabhau
english: Then both Śatrughna and Bharata, dejected and exhausted, writhed upon the ground like two bulls with broken horns.

sanskrit: tataḥ prakṛtimān vaidyaḥ pitur eṣāṃ purohitaḥ vasiṣṭho bharataṃ vākyam utthāpya tam uvāca ha
english: Then Vasiṣṭha, their father's family priest, composed and wise, raised Bharata up and spoke these words to him.

sanskrit: trīṇi dvandvāni bhūteṣu pravṛttāny aviśeṣataḥ teṣu cāparihāryeṣu naivaṃ bhavitum arhati
english: "Three pairs of opposites operate universally and without exception among all beings; and since these are unavoidable, you ought not to be thus prostrated."

sanskrit: sumantraś cāpi śatrughnam utthāpyābhiprasādya ca śrāvayām āsa tattvajñaḥ sarvabhūtabhavābhavau
english: And Sumantra too, the knower of truth, raised Śatrughna up, consoled him, and caused him to hear of the arising and passing away of all beings.

sanskrit: utthitau tau naravyāghrau prakāśete yaśasvinau varṣātapapariklinnau pṛthag indradhvajāv iva
english: The two tigers among men rose up, those illustrious ones, and appeared — drenched by rain and heat — like two separate banners of Indra.

sanskrit: aśrūṇi parimṛdnantau raktākṣau dīnabhāṣiṇau amātyās tvarayanti sma tanayau cāparāḥ kriyāḥ
english: Wiping away their tears, their eyes reddened, speaking in mournful tones, the ministers urged the two sons toward the remaining funerary observances.

sanskrit: atra yātrāṃ samīhantaṃ śatrughno lakṣmaṇānujaḥ bharataṃ śokasaṃtaptam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Then Śatrughna, younger brother of Lakṣmaṇa, spoke these words to Bharata, who was consumed by grief and was planning the journey.

sanskrit: gatir yaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ duḥkhe kiṃ punar ātmanaḥ sa rāmaḥ sattva saṃpannaḥ striyā pravrājito vanam
english: "He who is the refuge of all beings in their distress — how much more then of ourselves — that Rāma, endowed with every virtue, has been sent to the forest by a woman."

sanskrit: balavān vīrya saṃpanno lakṣmaṇo nāma yo 'py asau kiṃ na mocayate rāmaṃ kṛtvāpi pitṛnigraham
english: "And that Lakṣmaṇa — powerful and endowed with valour — why does he not free Rāma, even at the cost of restraining their father?"

sanskrit: pūrvam eva tu nigrāhyaḥ samavekṣya nayānayau utpathaṃ yaḥ samārūḍho nāryā rājā vaśaṃ gataḥ
english: "Indeed, he who had taken a crooked path, fallen under the dominion of a woman — the king — ought to have been restrained from the very beginning, weighing what was right and wrong."

sanskrit: iti saṃbhāṣamāṇe tu śatrughne lakṣmaṇānuje prāgdvāre 'bhūt tadā kubjā sarvābharaṇabhūṣitā
english: While Śatrughna, younger brother of Lakṣmaṇa, was speaking thus, Mantharā the hunchback appeared at that moment at the eastern gate, adorned with every ornament.

sanskrit: liptā candanasāreṇa rājavastrāṇi bibhratī mekhalā dāmabhiś citrai rajjubaddheva vānarī
english: Anointed with the finest sandalwood paste, wearing royal garments, garlanded about her waist with bright and variegated strings of ornaments, she looked like a monkey tied with a rope.

sanskrit: tāṃ samīkṣya tadā dvāḥstho bhṛśaṃ pāpasya kāriṇīm gṛhītvākaruṇaṃ kubjāṃ śatrughnāya nyavedayat
english: The doorkeeper, seeing that perpetrator of grave sin, seized the hunchback without mercy and reported her to Śatrughna.

sanskrit: yasyāḥ kṛte vane rāmo nyastadehaś ca vaḥ pitā seyaṃ pāpā nṛśaṃsā ca tasyāḥ kuru yathāmati
english: "On whose account Rāma is in the forest and your father has laid down his body — this is that wicked and cruel woman. Do with her as you see fit."

sanskrit: śatrughnaś ca tad ājñāya vacanaṃ bhṛśaduḥkhitaḥ antaḥpuracarān sarvān ity uvāca dhṛtavrataḥ
english: Śatrughna, steadfast in his vows and deeply aggrieved, upon learning of this spoke thus to all the inhabitants of the inner apartments.

sanskrit: tīvram utpāditaṃ duḥkhaṃ bhrātṝṇāṃ me tathā pituḥ yayā seyaṃ nṛśaṃsasya karmaṇaḥ phalam aśnutām
english: "She by whom such intense suffering has been inflicted upon my brothers and my father — let her now reap the fruit of that cruel act."

sanskrit: evam uktā ca tenāśu sakhī janasamāvṛtā gṛhītā balavat kubjā sā tadgṛham anādayat
english: Thus addressed by him, Mantharā, surrounded by her circle of companions, was seized with great force and made the inner chamber resound with her cries.

sanskrit: tataḥ subhṛśa saṃtaptas tasyāḥ sarvaḥ sakhījanaḥ kruddham ājñāya śatrughnaṃ vyapalāyata sarvaśaḥ
english: Then all her companions, deeply alarmed, perceiving Śatrughna's fury, fled in every direction.

sanskrit: amantrayata kṛtsnaś ca tasyāḥ sarvasakhījanaḥ yathāyaṃ samupakrānto niḥśeṣaṃ naḥ kariṣyati
english: And all the companions of Mantharā conferred together, saying: "This one, having begun thus, will utterly destroy every one of us."

sanskrit: sānukrośāṃ vadānyāṃ ca dharmajñāṃ ca yaśasvinīm kausalyāṃ śaraṇaṃ yāmaḥ sā hi no 'stu dhruvā gatiḥ
english: "Let us take refuge with Kausalyā, who is compassionate, generous, versed in dharma, and illustrious — for she shall be our unfailing refuge."

sanskrit: sa ca roṣeṇa tāmrākṣaḥ śatrughnaḥ śatrutāpanaḥ vicakarṣa tadā kubjāṃ krośantīṃ pṛthivītale
english: And Śatrughna, that scorcher of enemies, his eyes reddened with fury, then dragged the shrieking hunchback across the ground.

sanskrit: tasyā hy ākṛṣyamāṇāyā mantharāyās tatas tataḥ citraṃ bahuvidhaṃ bhāṇḍaṃ pṛthivyāṃ tad vyaśīryata
english: As Mantharā was being dragged hither and thither, her colourful ornaments of many kinds were scattered and broken upon the ground.

sanskrit: tena bhāṇḍena saṃkīrṇaṃ śrīmadrājaniveśanam aśobhata tadā bhūyaḥ śāradaṃ gaganaṃ yathā
english: The splendid royal residence, strewn with those scattered ornaments, shone all the more brightly then, like the autumnal sky.

sanskrit: sa balī balavat krodhād gṛhītvā puruṣarṣabhaḥ kaikeyīm abhinirbhartsya babhāṣe paruṣaṃ vacaḥ
english: That bull among men, that powerful one, blazing with fury, seized Kaikeyī, threatened her harshly, and spoke rough words.

sanskrit: tair vākyaiḥ paruṣair duḥkhaiḥ kaikeyī bhṛśaduḥkhitā śatrughna bhayasaṃtrastā putraṃ śaraṇam āgatā
english: Stricken to the quick by those harsh and painful words, Kaikeyī, greatly distressed and terrified of Śatrughna, came to her son for refuge.

sanskrit: tāṃ prekṣya bharataḥ kruddhaṃ śatrughnam idam abravīt avadhyāḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ pramadāḥ kṣamyatām iti
english: Seeing her, Bharata spoke to the wrathful Śatrughna: "Women are inviolable to all beings — let it be forgiven."

sanskrit: hanyām aham imāṃ pāpāṃ kaikeyīṃ duṣṭacāriṇīm yadi māṃ dhārmiko rāmo nāsūyen mātṛghātakam
english: "I would slay this wicked Kaikeyī, this evil-doer, were it not that righteous Rāma would reproach a matricide."

sanskrit: imām api hatāṃ kubjāṃ yadi jānāti rāghavaḥ tvāṃ ca māṃ caiva dharmātmā nābhibhāṣiṣyate dhruvam
english: "And if Rāghava were to learn that this hunchback too had been slain, that dharma-souled one would surely never speak to you or to me again."

sanskrit: bharatasya vacaḥ śrutvā śatrughno lakṣmaṇānujaḥ nyavartata tato roṣāt tāṃ mumoca ca mantharām
english: Hearing the words of Bharata, Śatrughna, younger brother of Lakṣmaṇa, desisted from his fury and released Mantharā.

sanskrit: sā pādamūle kaikeyyā mantharā nipapāta ha niḥśvasantī suduḥkhārtā kṛpaṇaṃ vilalāpa ca
english: Mantharā fell at the feet of Kaikeyī, gasping, tormented by intense pain, and lamented pitifully.

sanskrit: śatrughnavikṣepavimūḍhasaṃjñāṃ samīkṣya kubjāṃ bharatasya mātā śanaiḥ samāśvāsayad ārtarūpāṃ krauñcīṃ vilagnām iva vīkṣamāṇām
english: Seeing the hunchback, whose senses had been scattered and stunned by Śatrughna's rough handling, Bharata's mother gently consoled her — who had the appearance of one in distress, like a female krauñca bird clinging in desperation as she watched.
